name: Raptor Scheduled Content Expiry
author: Amr Issa

sections.description:
Raptor Scheduled Content Expiry gives you full control over what happens to your content when it reaches its expiration date. Set precise expiry dates on posts, pages, and custom post types, then choose from multiple expiry actions: auto-unpublish (move to draft), redirect to any URL, swap the content with a replacement, or simply hide it from visitors.

What You Can Do (Free)

  • Set expiry dates and times on any post, page, public custom post type, or WooCommerce product
  • Choose an expiry action per post: move to draft, redirect (301 or 302), swap content, or hide from visitors
  • Content swap lets you prepare a replacement message, archived notice, or seasonal placeholder
  • Auto-redirect expired URLs to any destination so visitors never hit a dead page
  • A Minimum Capability setting controls who can create, change or run expiry rules (Contributors and above by default)
  • Timezone-aware scheduling that respects your WordPress timezone setting
  • Audit log showing every expiry event with timestamp, action taken, and which user configured it
  • Quick Edit and Bulk Edit support for setting or clearing expiry dates across multiple posts
  • Dashboard widget showing upcoming expirations in the next 7 days
  • Clean uninstall: deleting the plugin removes its settings, expiry rules, audit log and queued jobs on every site
  • Runs on Action Scheduler for reliable, precise execution
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/raptor-scheduled-content-expiry, or install through the WordPress Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to Content Expiry > Settings in the admin sidebar to configure defaults and choose which post types to enable.
  4. Edit any post, page, custom post type, or WooCommerce product, and find the Content Expiry meta box to set expiry rules.
sections.faq:
Where do I find the plugin?

After activation, look for Content Expiry as a top-level item in the WordPress admin sidebar (clock icon). It contains two screens:

  • Settings — defaults, post-type opt-in, capability gate, dashboard widget toggle, log retention, and the Audit Log tab.
  • Scheduled Actions — a focused queue view showing only this plugin’s expiry jobs, with per-row Run Now / Cancel controls.

Who can manage expiry rules?

The Minimum Capability setting in Content Expiry > Settings decides who can see the meta box, Quick Edit and Bulk Edit fields and the Expiry column, and who can save, extend or run rules:

  • Contributor and above (edit_posts, the default)
  • Author and above (publish_posts)
  • Administrator only (manage_options)

Users also need permission to edit the specific post. Developers can override the capability with the smcexp_manage_capability filter.

What does “Hide from Visitors” do?

When the rule runs, the post stays published but visitors who cannot manage expiry rules get a 404 for it. It is also left out of front-end lists and search, the public REST API, oEmbed and sitemaps. Users who can manage expiry rules can still view it.

Does this work with custom post types?

Yes. Any public custom post type can be enabled in Content Expiry > Settings. Once enabled, the meta box, list-table column, Quick Edit, Bulk Edit, and front-end actions all work on that post type.

Developers can add private CPTs to the settings checkbox list via the smcexp_supported_post_types_choices filter, and override the runtime list via smcexp_supported_post_types.

Does this work with WooCommerce products?

Yes. Enable Products in Content Expiry > Settings and the Content Expiry meta box will appear in the WooCommerce product editor alongside the standard product fields. Quick Edit and Bulk Edit on the products list table work too.

How do I see what’s scheduled to expire?

Open Content Expiry > Scheduled Actions. The page lists every queued expiry job with the post title, action type (Move to Draft / Redirect / Swap / Hide), the time it fires (relative + absolute, in your WP timezone), and a colour-coded status pill. Pending jobs have Run now and Cancel buttons. Filter by Upcoming / Completed / Failed / Cancelled / All.

What happens if I deactivate the plugin?

Deactivating stops all expiry actions: redirects, hidden posts and swapped content go back to normal, and queued expiry jobs are cancelled. Your rules are kept. When you reactivate, every pending rule is queued again, and rules whose date has already passed run on the next queue run.

Does this work with caching plugins?

Yes, but full-page caching plugins may serve stale content briefly after an expiry action runs. The plugin fires a smcexp_cache_purge action that caching plugins can hook into.

Can I undo an expiry action?

Draft: re-publish the post. Redirect: clear the expiry rule. Swap Content: original content is never overwritten — clear the rule to restore it. Hide: clear the rule and the post becomes visible again immediately.

Does this require WooCommerce?

No. Action Scheduler is bundled directly with the plugin.

Is there a REST API or WP-CLI?

Yes. REST routes (namespace smcexp/v1):

  • GET /wp-json/smcexp/v1/upcoming lists pending rules you can edit, soonest first. Parameters: post_type, limit (1-100, default 25), offset. Requires the Minimum Capability.
  • GET /wp-json/smcexp/v1/log returns the audit log, newest first. Parameters: post_id, status, limit (1-100, default 25), offset. Requires manage_options.
  • POST /wp-json/smcexp/v1/expire/<id> runs a pending rule now. Requires the Minimum Capability and permission to edit the post.
  • POST /wp-json/smcexp/v1/extend/<id> with days (1-3650) moves a pending rule’s date later. Same permissions as expire.

WP-CLI commands:

  • wp smcexp list [--status=<pending|expired|cancelled|failed|all>] [--post_type=<type>] [--before=<date>] [--after=<date>] [--format=<table|json|csv|yaml|count|ids>]
  • wp smcexp expire <post_id> [--force] [--dry-run] runs a pending rule now. --force re-runs a rule that already ran, failed or was cancelled. Trashed posts are never touched.
  • wp smcexp extend <post_id> --days=<days> moves a pending rule’s date later by 1-3650 days.
  • wp smcexp log [--post_id=<id>] [--status=<status>] [--limit=<n>] [--format=<format>]

Run wp help smcexp <command> for details.
sections.changelog:
1.10.0

Tested with WordPress 7.1. Bundles Action Scheduler 4.2.0, so WordPress 6.9 or later is now required.

Security and permissions

  • Fixed: the Minimum Capability setting was saved but never enforced, so Authors and Contributors could create, extend and run expiry rules (including off-site redirects) even with “Administrator only” selected. It now applies to the meta box, list column, Quick Edit, Bulk Edit, the REST API and the hidden-post bypass.
  • Fixed: hidden (“Hide from Visitors”) posts were readable by anonymous visitors through the core REST API, REST search, WooCommerce Store API product lists and oEmbed.
  • Fixed: the dashboard widget was shown to every role, including Subscribers, and listed titles of draft and private posts.
  • Fixed: the Scheduled Actions screen accepted any Action Scheduler action ID, so other plugins’ jobs could be run or cancelled from it.

Scheduling reliability

  • Fixed: pending rules created on 1.0.0 were never queued. Pending rules without a queued job are now queued again automatically after an update or reactivation, so there is no need to re-save posts.
  • Fixed: deactivation did not cancel any queued jobs, and reactivation never re-queued them, so expiries were silently lost when WooCommerce or another Action Scheduler host was active. Deactivation now cancels the plugin’s jobs, and reactivation re-queues every pending rule.
  • Fixed: re-publishing or re-saving an expired post re-armed the old rule, which undid the documented “re-publish the post” undo.
  • Fixed: failures were recorded as completed, PHP errors skipped the retry, and a permanent failure left the rule pending forever. Failed rules are now retried once and then marked Failed.
  • Fixed: concurrent saves could leave two pending jobs for one post, and a stale job could expire a post early.
  • Fixed: Quick Edit scheduled a stray expiry job for the revision it created.
  • Fixed: multisite network activation set up only the main site, sites created later had no defaults, and network deactivation cleaned up only the main site.
  • Fixed: uninstall left the plugin’s Action Scheduler jobs, logs and group, and its transients, on every site.
  • Fixed: deactivation left Action Scheduler’s queue-runner cron event behind, which logged an invalid_schedule error.
  • Fixed: the audit-log prune event was rescheduled on every request, which triggered WooCommerce’s “translation loading too early” notice.

Editor, Quick Edit and Bulk Edit

  • Fixed: Bulk Edit never saved expiry rules.
  • Fixed: meta box validation errors and the past-date notice were never shown, so invalid rules were dropped while the editor reported success.
  • Fixed: a malformed expiry date caused a critical error in the meta box and Quick Edit save paths.
  • Fixed: Quick Edit skipped validation and could schedule Redirect or Swap rules with no URL or content.
  • Fixed: changing only the date in Quick Edit was ignored.
  • Fixed: legitimate redirect destinations, including the Default Redirect URL, were rejected. A redirect to the post’s own URL, which looped forever, is now refused.
  • Fixed: the Default Expiry Action and Default Redirect URL settings were saved but never used.
  • Fixed: the audit log lost “configured by” for rules set through Quick Edit, Bulk Edit or the REST API.
  • Fixed: duplicate element IDs and a broken label layout in the Quick Edit and Bulk Edit fields.

Front end

  • Fixed: hidden posts still appeared in Query Loop blocks, sticky posts, previous/next links, WooCommerce related products, sitemaps (core and Yoast) and feeds.
  • Fixed: Administrators and Editors also got a 404 for hidden posts.
  • Fixed: expired hidden WooCommerce products could still be bought.
  • Fixed: Swap Content applied only on single views; it now also applies to excerpts, archives, feeds and the REST API, with paragraphs, shortcodes and blocks rendered.
  • Improved: the hidden-post filter no longer adds postmeta joins to every front-end query.

Admin screens

  • Fixed: Run now and Cancel on the Scheduled Actions screen caused “headers already sent” warnings and a blank page.
  • Fixed: cancelling a job from Scheduled Actions left the rule marked pending and wrote no audit entry.
  • Fixed: the Settings page showed no “Settings saved.” confirmation or validation errors.
  • Fixed: saving settings while WooCommerce or another post-type provider was inactive silently disabled expiry for that post type.
  • Fixed: on phones, the Scheduled Actions table hid the columns with Run now and Cancel.
  • Fixed: admin styles were not loaded on Scheduled Actions in translated admin languages.
  • Fixed: settings controls had no accessible names.
  • Fixed: the audit log and list column showed raw UTC timestamps and untranslated slugs.
  • Fixed: dashboard widget data was not refreshed when rules changed, and its “View full audit log” link pointed to an old URL.
  • Fixed: PHP 8.1+ deprecation notices and empty links when a post has no edit link.
  • Fixed: Action Scheduler’s own Tools > Scheduled Actions page is no longer removed, so WooCommerce and other plugins keep their queue view and the linked raw queue page renders correctly.
  • Fixed: an uncached per-row database query on the Scheduled Actions screen.
  • Changed: meta box accent colours follow the WordPress 7 admin colour scheme.
  • Fixed: a translatable string without a translators comment.

REST API and WP-CLI

  • Fixed: /extend and wp smcexp extend accepted negative, zero, non-numeric and huge day values. Days must now be 1-3650, and only pending rules can be extended.
  • Fixed: /expire and wp smcexp expire reported success for posts without a pending rule and left the queued job behind, and the CLI restored trashed posts. Both now run only pending rules (--force re-runs a finished rule) and cancel the queued job first.
  • Fixed: /upcoming left out scheduled and private posts, reported a total that included posts you cannot see, had no limit cap and was not ordered by expiry. It now also returns expiry_date_local.
  • Fixed: permission errors returned 401 to logged-in users and for unknown posts. They now return 403 and 404.
  • Fixed: wp smcexp list --format=ids printed “Array”. Help text now lists one option per entry, unknown IDs report “not found”, and list gained --before and --after.
  • Removed: the unused smcexp_bulk_edit_save admin-ajax endpoint.

Compatibility

  • Updated: bundled Action Scheduler 3.9.3 to 4.2.0, which includes hardening against unsafe deserialization of stored schedules. Requires at least WordPress 6.9.
  • Changed: the “Action Scheduler could not be loaded” notice no longer tells site owners to run Composer.
  • Fixed: the audit table definition caused a no-op schema change on MariaDB.
  • Docs: corrected the readme, documented the REST API and WP-CLI commands, and fixed the WP-CLI command name in the changelog (wp smcexp, not wp scem).

1.9.1

  • Fixed: clicking “Run now” on a pending row in the Scheduled Actions screen executed the expiry but left the Action Scheduler row stuck as “Pending”. The handler now routes through Action Scheduler’s queue runner, which fires the expiry hook and marks the row complete in the AS store, so the row correctly moves to the Completed tab on reload.

1.9.0

Scheduling reliability

  • Fixed: bundled Action Scheduler was not initialising on fresh installs because it was loaded inside a plugins_loaded priority-0 callback, which prevented Action Scheduler’s own bootstrap hooks (added during the same priority) from firing. Result: as_schedule_single_action() was undefined when posts were saved, so expiries were silently never queued. Action Scheduler is now loaded at plugin-file load time.
  • Fixed: the “Action Scheduler could not be loaded” admin notice was being shown spuriously because the availability check ran at plugins_loaded priority 0 — before Action Scheduler defines its helper functions at priority 1. The check now runs at priority 20.
  • Fixed: timezone handling treated the WordPress timezone as UTC whenever the site was configured with a UTC offset (gmt_offset) instead of a named zone (timezone_string). Local times like “12:44 PM” were being saved as 12:44 UTC, causing actions to fire hours late. Both the meta-box save path and the Quick/Bulk Edit save path now use wp_timezone(), which handles named zones and UTC offsets correctly.

Custom post types & WooCommerce products

  • Added: full support for any public custom post type once it’s enabled in Content Expiry > Settings. Bulk-edit “Expiry” column hooks now register dynamically per post type (manage_{post_type}_posts_columns / manage_{post_type}_posts_custom_column) instead of the legacy blanket hooks, so the column only appears on post types you actually opted into.
  • Added: WooCommerce product support. The meta box appears in the WooCommerce classic product editor; Quick Edit and Bulk Edit work on the products list table.
  • Added: smcexp_supported_post_types_choices filter, letting developers add private CPTs to the settings checkbox list.
  • Changed: the Media (attachment) post type is no longer offered in the settings list (rarely useful for content expiry; can be re-added via the new filter).

Admin UX

  • Changed: Content Expiry is now a top-level menu item in the admin sidebar (clock icon) with two children — Settings and Scheduled Actions — instead of living under Tools.
  • Added: a custom Scheduled Actions screen replaces the raw Action Scheduler queue UI for end users. It shows only this plugin’s jobs with friendly action labels, post links, relative + absolute times, status pills, tab filters (Upcoming / Completed / Failed / Cancelled / All) with accurate counts, and per-row Run Now / Cancel buttons for pending jobs. A footer link still opens the raw Action Scheduler queue for power users.
  • Improved: the Content Expiry meta box has been redesigned to match the Gutenberg sidebar’s visual language — uppercase 11px field labels, polished inputs with focus rings, a custom select arrow, a colour-coded status pill (Pending / Expired / Cancelled), grouped subgroup panels for the Redirect and Swap Content fields, and a separated, de-emphasised “Clear expiry rule” row.
  • Improved: clicking anywhere inside the date/time field opens the date picker (previously only the calendar icon was clickable). Uses HTMLInputElement.showPicker() with a graceful fallback.

1.0.0

  • Initial release
  • Post, page, and custom post type expiry with date/time picker
  • Four expiry actions: Draft, Redirect (301/302), Swap Content, Hide
  • Audit log with custom database table
  • Quick Edit and Bulk Edit support
  • Dashboard widget for upcoming expirations
  • REST API endpoints for developers
  • WP-CLI commands
  • Action Scheduler bundled (no WooCommerce dependency)
  • Full i18n support with .pot file
